title: Fix timestep in NHC subloop
body:
Closes https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/issues/1716

As @beidouamg pointed out, a timestep used in subloops of Nose-Hoover-chain thermostat integration was wrong.
This MR fixes it.

The original unittest checked forward n steps with `timestep` and backward 2n steps with `timestep/2`, but it appears this check was too tight for numerical error (or some undiscovered bug...).
This MR also changes the unittest to check forward n steps and backward n steps with the same timestep.

author: lan496

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I think the previous version of the test was stronger since it tests something physical (2 * half-a-time-step being the same as a time step, which is not trivial given the complexity of MD expressions).

Is there a reason we cannot do so anymore?

I don't want to ask for too much, but it might be worth thinking about an improvement of the test since something must have been incorrect about the previous implementation.  Any ideas?

Thanks a lot for the quick fix!

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: @schiotz do you have ideas for how to best test the propagation?

comments.author: lan496
comments.body: Honestly, I do not fully understand why the previous time integration tests failed. It seems _integrate_p_eta_j is very susceptible to numerical fluctuation, possibly due to multiplication by exp (self._p_eta[j] *= np.exp(...)). If we set a tiny value for timestep, the previous time integration tests would pass, but it does not fully capture an algorithm implementation error in turn...

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
One step of length dt should always be equivalent to two steps of dt/2 if dt is small enough right?  The thermostat should only have a very small effect.  Maybe we could test that (on *all* MD classes actually, some day) using randomized velocities/positions, and a quite strict precision.  That way, we verify some physical promise about local (in time) correctness.

That the MD propagation produces the correct long-term dynamics is of course a more difficult question, but I'd be quite happy if we could test something meaningful for an individual step, since we often have very coarse criteria in the longer tests and they may not detect problems that the dt/2 test could.

Please feel free to discuss.

comments.author: lan496
comments.body:
> One step of length dt should always be equivalent to two steps of dt/2 if dt is small enough right?

Yes. Let U(dt) be a true time integrator from the Nose-Hoover equations. The current implementation, say U_{sym}(dt), should satisfies U(dt) - U_{sym}(dt) = O(dt^3). 
So, if dt is sufficiently small, we expect U_{sym}(dt/2)^2 ~ U(dt) ~ U_{sym}(dt) 

> I'd be quite happy if we could test something meaningful for an individual step

That's right! I will think about another unit test for this MR

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
I think it is very useful to test details of the propagation of both the MD and the thermostat, when possible and applicable, for example by checking that two half timesteps do the same as one big - we just need to remember that we are testing very small changes here, so maybe it is better to test that 20 half steps does the same as 10 whole.

In addition, once these new MD algorithms started to get added to ASE, I decided it was time to add proper tests of their longer-time properties.  But those tests are slow, as they require statistics.  I therefore added them to Asap and marked them as slow tests, so they are run every Saturday on Niflheim.

The tests check that temperatures and pressures approach the right values as the simulation proceeds, but also that they approach the right values with *roughly* the right rate.  For NHC, the rate is not checked as NHC is known for being good at maintaining the right ensemble, but not for approaching it from afar - oscillations tend to appear in the auxillary variables that take a long time to die out.

In addition, with dynamics that claim to reproduce the canonical ensemble (NVT), it is checked that the fluctuations in T are correct.

With the NpT ensembles, the tests are a bit more relaxed since the barostat and the thermostat interact, so equilibrium is reached a little bit slower than the timescales seem to indicate.  Also, I consistently observe slightly too large fluctuations in both T and p, but not as bad as in some of the older dynamics, where the fluctuations are all wrong.

comments.author: lan496
comments.body:
I have added a new unit test for NoseHooverChainThermostat,  https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/merge_requests/3768/diffs?commit_id=64f8f63ee0c0c61c0b4a890743e06b1ead6ee70b .
This test compares NoseHooverChainThermostat with delta by n steps and that with delta/2 with 2n steps. The difference between the two time integrations should decrease by delta until rounding errors are reached. 
Although the current implementation passes the test, the previous wrong equation before this MR also looks to pass the test due to the small coefficient changes...

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Thanks a lot @lan496 and all.  I'll go ahead and merge this.

Should there be a release note?  "Fixed bug in Nose-Hoover chain thermostat which would [...description of bug...]"?

comments.author: lan496
comments.body: Yes, something like "Fixed bug in Nose-Hoover chain thermostat which would inconsistently update extended variables for the thermostat."

comments.body:
Unfortunately on one of my machines (and one of the CAMD runners) the test will fail:

```

E        +    where <function allclose at 0x12f9035558b0> = np.allclose
E        +    and   array([ 3.76773741e-06, -3.68151289e-07,  4.05009980e-07]) = <ase.md.nose_hoover_chain.NoseHooverChainThermostat object at 0x12f8f4288100>._p_eta

/home/askhl/src/ase/ase/test/md/test_nose_hoover_chain.py:66: AssertionError
```

It seems like a simple tolerance problem, so I will simply make it less strict and merge immediately.

Please let me know if anything better can be done about it.

(I notice that `p_eta_start` is simply zeros.  I assume that's meant to be so.)
